The Mystery School corpus: Boole, Cosmos, the Metamorphosis of Plants and Jung's chapter X (RDR-030, PR 4)
The Mystery School corpus: the web adapters, 20 texts and the Latin at the Gate (RDR-030, PR 3)

The Mystery School's complete library: investigation and design (RDR-030)

beats.say: This week Sophia moved more smoothly, the Mystery School became a full library, and the Image Stream got its first parts.
In RISE Live, Sophia's frame transitions now move as one gesture. The eye shuts once between frames, and she glides on an arc while the face draws in step.
Traces on a real graphics card found the faults. The eye used to reopen between two frames, and the face drew a frame behind.
Going from the shell to the full frame is now one gesture that only shrinks. From the cut to rest, it dropped from 2.83 seconds to 2.37.
A closing frame now draws in from the first moment of the cut. A new visual changes only while the eye is shut.
The Mystery School is now a pane in the Library. It is a wheel with the Gate at the centre and seven houses around it, and a lectern beside it reads whatever the wheel points at.
It holds 66 texts, and only four were readable at the start. Each text shows one of three honest states: readable, carried but not served, or not yet carried.
Then the corpus grew. Ten Standard Ebooks texts came first, then twenty-four from Project Gutenberg, taking the school from four readable texts to fourteen, then thirty-eight.

New readers for the web brought in twenty more, the Gate's Latin among them. Boole, Humboldt's Cosmos, Goethe's Metamorphosis of Plants and a chapter of Jung followed, after conversion or a proofing pass.
Kapp and Ibn Khaldun arrived as proofed selections. Haeckel's hundred plates arrived as a picture work, where each unit is one plate.

The Gate now reads Pico's Oration in RISE's English draft, with the Latin after it. A model made the draft from the Latin alone, and no person has yet read it against the Latin. Kepler's Harmonices Mundi, Book V, is readable in Latin as six units. The Futurist Manifesto, in French and in English, was the last text, so all 66 are readable. A person has still to read the proofing diffs.
A separate piece of work began: the Image Stream. Its core is a flash meter that measures the light a stream puts on the screen, and a clock of four to twelve images a second.

Its presenter is a canvas of at most 140 pixels, behind a flag that is off. No reader can reach it, and flashing stays off. The meter judges every frame, and any trip hands the space back to the Gallery.
Plus listeners can now replay retained private audio across devices. The same verified Plus identity, text and voice reuse the audio with no new provider call and no new debit.
Checkout remains disabled, and no live provider call is claimed.
